meaning: The plotting deck is driven by exactly two named seeds, :m3_basinA and :m3_basinB, each settled to steady state and then run through the tilt solve. This fixes which two basins are compared side by side in every downstream panel.

could_move.what: Which pair of basins the tilt figures contrast; any other seed in seed_defs is silently excluded
Initial condition of each dynamic run, since u0_ss comes from settling that seed's mV/mC/mQ
Panels that use the live probe `comps` rather than the per-basin comps_dyn may mix scopes
Tilt/postural panels built from these two runs
Cross-model comparison deck, if it reuses these basin runs
Steady-state deck, which depends on the settled states

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: restricting to two seeds narrows the comparison. If the two seeds do not sit in genuinely distinct basins, the figures show two near-identical curves instead of bistability. I cannot tell from this context which it is.

check.why: Runs only the two settle-plus-tilt solves and prints their retcodes, so you can see whether both basins solve and stay distinct, without a re-fit.
